s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of generalized skin lesions and jaundice following a surgical procedure
salient_findings: Fever following removal of a tibial implant
Development of pruritus and fluid-filled rashes after antibiotic use
key_facts: 22-year-old man
15-day history of generalized painful fluid-filled skin lesions
7 days of yellow scleral discoloration
1 month of fever following removal of a tibial implant
History of tibial fracture treated with internal fixation
Surgical-site infection and persistent fever after implant removal
Use of paracetamol and ciprofloxacin
Development of generalized pruritus and fluid-filled rashes after ciprofloxacin use
Denial of angioedema, dyspnea, abdominal distention, lower-limb swelling, hematemesis, melena, altered sensorium, alcohol use, or immunocompromise
Afebrile with stable vital signs on examination
Icterus without pallor, clubbing, cyanosis, lymphadenopathy, or dehydration
Multiple generalized vesicles and bullae with non-hemorrhagic crusts on dermatologic examination
Mucosal findings including hemorrhagic lip crusts and penile erosion
Leukocyte count 18,520/mm3 with neutrophils 64%, lymphocytes 22%, and eosinophils 12%
Hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, platelets 423,000/mm3
Elevated liver enzymes and total bilirubin

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Generalized painful fluid-filled skin lesions and mucosal involvement after ciprofloxacin use

shortlist.label: DRESS syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Fever, rash, and systemic involvement following ciprofloxacin use, with elevated liver enzymes and eosinophilia

shortlist.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe skin lesions and mucosal involvement after ciprofloxacin use, with potential for high mortality

shortlist.label: Drug-induced liver injury
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated liver enzymes and jaundice following ciprofloxacin use, with potential for severe liver damage

shortlist.label: Severe cutaneous adverse reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Generalized skin lesions and systemic involvement after ciprofloxacin use, with potential for severe morbidity and mortality
